userStories.title: Expose the OS sandbox availability probe as a CLI command
acceptanceCriteria: When `probe` resolves `{ available: true }` and `platform` returns `darwin`, then the document logged by `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` deep-equals `{ backend: 'srt', platform: 'darwin', available: true }`.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: true }`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` returns `0`.

When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'sandbox ran a command but did not enforce a write deny' }` and `platform` returns `linux`, then the document logged by `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` deep-equals `{ backend: 'srt', platform: 'linux', available: false, reason: 'sandbox ran a command but did not enforce a write deny' }`.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'x' }`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` returns `1`.

When `probe` rejects with `new Error('module not found')`, then the document logged by `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` has `available: false` and `reason: 'sandbox probe failed: module not found'`.
When `probe` rejects with `new Error('module not found')`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` returns `1`.
When `probe` rejects with the string `boom`, then the document logged by `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` has `reason: 'sandbox probe failed: boom'`.
When `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` runs, then `_sandboxProbeCmdDeps.createBackend` is called exactly once with an argument deep-equal to `DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG.network`.
When `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` runs, then `_sandboxProbeCmdDeps.probe` is called exactly once with the backend object `createBackend` returned.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: true }`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` calls the backend's `reset` exactly once.
When `probe` rejects, then `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` calls the backend's `reset` exactly once.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: true }` and the backend's `reset` rejects with `new Error('reset failed')`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` returns `0`.

When `probe` resolves `{ available: true }` and the backend's `reset` rejects with `new Error('reset failed')`, then the document logged by `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` has `available: true`.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'x' }`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` calls `_sandboxProbeCmdDeps.log` exactly once.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'x' }`, then the string `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` logs contains no ESC (`\u001b`) character.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: true }` and `platform` returns `darwin`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({})` logs exactly `Sandbox (srt, darwin): available`.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'no bwrap' }` and `platform` returns `linux`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({})` logs exactly `Sandbox (srt, linux): unavailable: no bwrap`.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'no bwrap' }`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({})` returns `1`.
When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'no bwrap' }`, then `sandboxProbeCommand({})` calls `_sandboxProbeCmdDeps.log` exactly once.
When `sandboxProbeCommand` is imported from `@/cli` and `probe` resolves `{ available: true }`, then calling it with no argument returns `0`.
Given the live sandbox suite's own probe reports the sandbox available, when `bun bin/nax.ts sandbox probe --json` is spawned from the repository root, then it exits with code `0`.

Given the live sandbox suite's own probe reports the sandbox available, when `bun bin/nax.ts sandbox probe --json` is spawned from the repository root, then its stdout parses as JSON with `available: true` and `backend: 'srt'`.

When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'platform linux is not supported by the srt sandbox' }` for an unsupported platform, then the document logged by `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` has `reason: 'platform linux is not supported by the srt sandbox'`.

When `probe` resolves `{ available: false, reason: 'sandbox could not run a command: exit 1' }` for a command that cannot run, then the document logged by `sandboxProbeCommand({ json: true })` has `reason: 'sandbox could not run a command: exit 1'`.

routing.reasoning: Additive CLI handler plus barrel and Commander wiring follow existing auth patterns; the subprocess live check isolates srt's singleton, so there is no new abstraction or cross-module sandbox change and a single-session TDD pass suffices.

modifiedFiles.reason: gains the two live `nax sandbox probe` cases inside its existing `describe.skipIf(!probe.available)` block; no existing case or assertion in the file changes.

analysis: Existing TypeScript/Bun/Commander CLI; additive command, no migration or change to current sandbox behavior. src/sandbox/probe.ts:27-68 exports probeSandbox(backend), checking platform support before creating a temp directory, wrapping a command and verifying both an allowed-write marker and a denied-write marker; only runArgv is bounded by PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=30_000 (line 19). Its unavailable reasons include unsupported platform (line 29), wrapping failure (line 48), inability to run (lines 56-59), and missing enforcement (line 62). src/sandbox/srt-backend.ts:51-112 exports createSrtBackend(network), with lazy srt module loading/initialization (lines 57-71) and reset (lines 105-110); constructing the backend itself does not load srt. src/sandbox/types.ts:13,22,34-45 defines SandboxBackendName ('srt'), ProbeResult discriminated union and SandboxBackend.name/reset; src/sandbox/index.ts:22,32,34-45 re-exports required symbols. src/config/schemas-sandbox.ts:21-49 defines SandboxConfigSchema, open network when allowedDomains is absent (lines 39-44), and DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG parsed from {} (line 50); src/config/index.ts:109-110 re-exports SandboxConfig and DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG. src/sandbox/registry.ts:26-46 caches its probe per process and uses the run logger; its rejected-probe wording is `sandbox probe failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` (lines 38-41). Do not call the registry: a CLI probe must run afresh and use a private backend, resetting it after success or rejection while ignoring reset errors. src/cli/auth.ts:24-31 provides the mutable CLI log dependency seam; authListCommand at lines 176-206 demonstrates one-document JSON logging and exit-code-returning handler. src/cli/index.ts:1-25 is the barrel imported by bin/nax.ts:43-70; add the new handler and type exports there. bin/nax.ts:885-921 registers auth subcommands with Commander and process.exit(await ...); add sandbox probe adjacent to auth without dir/profile flags or config-loading calls. docs/guides/cli-reference.md:568-584 has the auth section and the insertion point before mcp. test/unit/cli/auth.test.ts:36-86 and test/unit/cli/auth-list.test.ts:62-92 illustrate saving/replacing/restoring mutable seams for Bun unit tests; new test/unit/cli/sandbox-probe.test.ts should stub all four command dependencies on every test, use a resolving reset spy by default, and avoid importing/loading the actual srt module. test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-live.test.ts:25-53 obtains the registry backend at module scope and gates its live cases with describe.skipIf(!probe.available); add two assertions using one subprocess spawn of `bun bin/nax.ts sandbox probe --json` from the repository root inside that block, each with 60_000ms timeout. Its process-wide srt manager is shared across Bun test files; never invoke the command handler in-process in this suite or reset the existing backend. Risks: stdout must have exactly one log call even on failure; JSON must be ANSI-free and omit reason when available; reset failure cannot override probe result; no reads of project/profile config; isolated subprocess avoids disrupting singleton; CLI barrel import cost is existing behavior. No data/schema migration or breaking interface is required; existing run-time registry and probe implementation remain unchanged.
outOfScope: A `--profile`, `-d` or config-driven probe: the command never reads `execution.sandbox` (including `enabled` and `network.allowedDomains`) from any config file, and always probes the default open-network srt backend.
Probing whether srt's network proxy starts under a restricted `network.allowedDomains` list.
Caching the probe result on disk or across invocations; every invocation probes afresh.
A timeout around srt's platform check, `initialize()` or `reset()`; only the wrapped probe command is bounded, by `PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`.
Any change to `probeSandbox`, `probeSandboxOnce`, the sandbox registry or `createSrtBackend`.
A timestamp field in the report; the consumer records when it probed.
